clue.text: Middle Eastern performance shaking corporation?

parts.note: surface reading: some show from the Middle East that rattles a big company
setter's reading: 'corporation' is an old jokey word for a paunch, and the dance consists of shaking it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but in older British slang it means a large stomach; the performer shakes that.
explanation.definitionFit: This Middle Eastern dance style is built around rolling and shaking movements of the stomach.

clue.text: Seen looking to the north in zodiac, a playful animal

indicators.note: in a down entry, facing north means reading upwards, so the run of letters is taken backwards
what is seen in a phrase is sitting visibly inside its letters, waiting to be spotted

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of zodiac, the word a and the start of playful

explanation.surface: A frisky creature is spotted heading north across the zodiac, like a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American domesticated camelid kept for its wool, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Country: capital in trouble, flag down also

indicators.note: a capital is a capital letter, the head letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of trouble
to flag down a taxi is to hail it
also means and, in addition

explanation.surface: A country's capital is in turmoil and its flag has been lowered too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'flag down' look political; one picks a first letter and the other means hail.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand is a Southeast Asian nation, so it is a country.

clue.text: Jolly intelligent

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'very intelligent' with jolly as British slang for very, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective can mean cheerful and sunny in mood, and also clever or smart.

clue.text: It's hard to get on with family member nursing cold

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a relative, a parent's brother
icy means very cold

explanation.surface: A relative who is unwell with a cold is difficult to get along with.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLE holds ICY: UN-ICY-CLE. 'Hard to get on with' reads as a difficult person, but here it means hard to mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-wheeled cycle is notoriously difficult to climb onto and stay balanced on.

clue.text: Crack in ground, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the phrase says the word is judged by how it is spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: ground underfoot is the floor; in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same

explanation.surface: A fissure in the earth, described as if it were sounded out.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaw is a defect, such as a crack in a gem or a piece of china.

clue.text: Secretive behaviour in the last novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are rebuilt into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A reader notes the sly, furtive conduct in an author's final book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a noun, the last book written, but it is the adjective signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is acting quietly and covertly so as not to be noticed, which is secretive conduct.

clue.text: Wash beneath right hand

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part placed beneath another comes after it

parts.note: to put things right is to put them straight; correct, honest
to flush is to wash out with a rush of water

explanation.surface: An instruction to clean underneath the right hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right hand' looks like a body part to scrub, but 'hand' alone is the definition, a set of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, five cards of the same suit in sequence make a strong hand of this name.

clue.text: Lock phone two ways

parts.note: to phone someone is to ring them

indicators.note: the same word is used twice, once read forwards and once read backwards

parts.note: TEL is the standard abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: A security instruction: secure the phone in two different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Phone is used twice: forwards as the verb to ring, then as the abbreviation TEL read backwards, giving LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair.

clue.text: Equestrian affair venerated, they fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A grand horse show that its devotees think highly of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as a verb, what they like, but it is the adjective signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-day event is a horse-riding competition combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping over successive days.

clue.text: Look to probe English university for charging again

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so one part goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: the University of Reading, in the English town of that name
lo is an old word for look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone investigates an English university's tuition fees, which keep going up.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a university town west of London. 'Charging' tempts as billing fees, but it means loading a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Reloading is putting fresh ammunition or a new charge into a weapon, so charging it again.

clue.text: In fear, crouch lower before Her Majesty

indicators.note: before places one part in front of the next in the answer

parts.note: something that lows, or moos, is a cow
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A frightened subject bows lower and lower before the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like the comparative of low, but read as low-er it is an animal that lows, a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to shrink down or cringe from fright, which is crouching in fear.

clue.text: Test team batting, help to make a comeback?

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A cricket side in trouble at the crease needs support to fight back.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, so a Test team is a national side.
explanation.definitionFit: India is one of the nations that plays Test cricket, so it names a Test team.

clue.text: Trimmings of kale alongside variety of haricot vegetable

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters appear in another arrangement

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

indicators.note: trimmings are what is cut from the edges, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of kale

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish: trimmed kale served next to some kind of haricot bean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alongside' lets the trimmed kale go after the rearranged bean, even though the clue names it first.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: An available choice, where cutlery placed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an option that is being offered or considered
second meaning, literal: knives and forks are laid on a dining surface

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means up for discussion or offered as an option; literally it is where you lay the knives and forks.

clue.text: With nothing to lose, chase cherry for big innings

indicators.note: nothing is the zero-shaped letter, and to lose it means taking it out

parts.note: to hound someone is to chase them
nothing, a zero, looks like the letter O
cherry is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A cricketer with nothing to lose attacks the cherry-red ball to make a big score.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's ball is often called the cherry, but here cherry is simply the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a century, a batter's score of one hundred runs, counts as a big innings.

clue.text: Comparable processes I reveal around opening of trial

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go on either side of another piece
to process material is to work it over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of trial

explanation.surface: A legal witness describes how they disclose procedures at the start of a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative means considered in comparison with something else, so it is a synonym for comparable.

clue.text: Mould precast in various ranges

indicators.note: to mould something is to reshape it, so the letters take on a new form

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Mould for precast concrete is sold in many sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' looks like a noun, a shape for casting, but it is the verb signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectra, the plural of spectrum, are ranges or scales of values, so plural ranges.

clue.text: Promising vigorous music, organ installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: swing is lively big-band jazz
the ear is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: Up-and-coming lively music with a church organ fitted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promising' looks like an adjective, full of potential, but it is the verb: giving one's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing is vowing or pledging solemnly, which is promising.

clue.text: Something electric, possibly, in country working independently

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a European country
an electric eel is one possible thing that is electric

explanation.surface: An electrical gadget, perhaps, abroad operating on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' admits the eel is only one example of something electric.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance is self-employed, taking work for several clients, so works independently.

clue.text: Dead equal or fewer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gone, no longer existing
second meaning: not exceeding, as in a number of items or less

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead equal' reads as exactly the same; the two words split into separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means ceased to exist, and also not more than a given amount, that is, equal or less.

clue.text: European plant with edible root

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a root vegetable, the rutabaga

explanation.walkthrough: A swede in Britain is the yellow root vegetable Americans call rutabaga.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a person from Sweden, and also a turnip-like vegetable grown for its root.

clue.text: Pound to secure vessel, barely enough

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, like a pigsty
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A dock must secure a ship, though it has hardly enough room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' tempts as money or weight, but it is an animal pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means meagre or insufficient, so hardly sufficient in amount.

clue.text: In poor condition, one accepting frailty at first

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a unit is one

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of frailty

explanation.surface: An unhealthy patient comes to terms with the first signs of weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means not physically in good shape, which is a poor condition.

clue.text: Superb penalty

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excellent, of high quality
second meaning: a sum of money paid as punishment

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for a penalty kick; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as an adjective for high quality and as a noun for a monetary punishment.

clue.text: Fruity thing me cuddling member, a youth

indicators.note: to cuddle is to wrap your arms around, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: taken as written
a limb, a member of the body
taken as written
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: An affectionate scene: me hugging a young member of the family, like a little sweetie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity thing' sounds like a flirtatious person, but it is a breakfast preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a preserve made from citrus fruit, so it is a fruity thing.

clue.text: Chinese dynasty finished in royal house

parts.note: the Han dynasty ruled China from 206 BC to AD 220
over means ended

explanation.surface: An ancient Chinese line of rulers came to an end within a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover was the German royal line that ruled Britain from George I to Victoria.

clue.text: Card revealed when turned over, bet initially lost

indicators.note: turning a word over flips it end to end, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to let on is to disclose a secret

indicators.note: its first letter is lost, so the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler's card game: the card shown when flipped means the wager is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' looks like a playing card in this gambling scene, but it is a small greetings card.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card with a printed design, used for short messages.
